articles.chapeau: A leak has narrowed the window for when the GTA 6 review embargo will end. The day and time matches past Rockstar launches, but some coverage may not appear until the release date. Journalists and content creators have also allegedly not yet received digital codes.
articles.txt:
Earlier GTA 6 leaks claimed the review embargo would expire in advance of the November 19th release date . The media reportedly can also expect copies of the Rockstar title before the end of October. Now, a poster with a history of accurate predictions has shared when Metacritic scores will surface.
While ResetEra contributor BlackBate isn’t well known, they have gradually built a reliable track record. Starting in 2021, the forum member revealed announcements for Microsoft Flight Simulator , Death Stranding , Pragmata , and Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced .
On October 23rd, BlackBate identified November 18th as when the GTA 6 review embargo will end. More specifically, Metacritic scores should go live at around 12:01-1:01 PM CET/6-7 AM EST. However, certain sites or YouTube channels may need to wait until 6:01 CET/12:01 AM EST on the November 19th launch day.
ⓘ BlackBate@ResetEra forums GTA 6 review embargo leak shown It’s unclear why some media members would have to delay their coverage until the GTA 6 release date. One theory is that Rockstar prefers written articles to appear first to establish a critical consensus. Then, videos, which may contain story spoilers, can show footage as it unlocks on the Xbox and PlayStation Store . Or the studio may simply prioritize journalists from larger publications.
With time running out, BlackBate also suspects fans won’t see hands-on previews . So far, content creators have been invited to watch gameplay but not control Jason and Lucia themselves.
Trusted insider NateTheHate leaked that Rockstar should soon distribute copies to the media. The ResetEra poster believes the studio hasn't dispatched the digital Xbox or PS5 codes . Their sources suggest that will happen either the week of October 26th or early in November. Testers could have anywhere from 2 to 3 weeks to explore Leonida's open world .
As with all leaks, followers should take the GTA 6 review embargo details with a grain of salt. Nevertheless, the claims are consistent with Grand Theft Auto 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 . In both cases, critical opinions emerged a day before launch.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is coming in just under a month. Yeah, that’s real. Pinch yourself if you need to… or check out the new launch trailer that Rockstar just dropped if you need confirmation that you’re not dreaming. Much less painful that way.
This new trailer focuses on dual protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, and gives us more insight into their backstories and bond than we’ve had up to this point. Yes, we’ve known for a while that the relationship between Jason and Lucia is a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style crime romance, but we have a little better sense now for what’s motivating the two.
“Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive.”
For Jason, we see how that deck is stacked against him when we learn that he left the army on poor terms – so bad that he can’t even get a loan! This is just speculation here, but maybe he wouldn’t be trying to rob people if he was able to do something normal and boring with a legitimate loan, like starting his own business. That’s a good thing for us, though, lest this turn into Grand Theft Entrepreneur (okay wait, that game might kinda slap actually).
In any case, being ex-military has presumably left Jason with a lot of deadly combat training without much to do with it. Idle hands being the devil’s plaything, it’s no surprise that we see him in the trailer go from waxing boats to wearing night vision goggles and shooting sniper rifles, suggesting there might be a little hint of Splinter Cell in this GTA formula this time around.
We don’t learn a ton about Lucia, herself, in this trailer, but it doesn’t shy from showing her hot and steamy relationship moments with Jason – literally so in the case of a romantic shower kiss where we can see a flashing ankle monitor on Lucia’s leg, serving as a subtle reminder that, for all the ways crime pays for this duo, the law is never too far behind.
And on that note, paradise is certainly not without trouble in this story, as we see interspersed between the shots of gorgeous sunset vistas, cruising in expensive luxury cars, and a few exotic reptiles are shots of tense police chases, helicopter explosions, and Lucia in a shaky voice saying, “are we gonna be okay?” Time will tell on that one, but if one thing’s for sure, it’s gonna be a hell of a time.
Of course, I have to mention that this game is absolutely stunning. Sweat glistens, smoke billows, lizards are… lizarding. Rockstar have said that all the footage we see in the trailer was captured entirely in-game on a PS5™ console, which means it’s probably going to look just as crisp and detailed on your home setup as it does in the trailer.
The soundtrack is going to be amazing too, evidenced by the catchy original single we hear throughout the trailer, “Flower in a Hurricane” by Justice and featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard. There are many more famous artists who have leant their talents to GTA 6, including Travis Scott, Yung Lean, Future, Metro Boomin, and even Keith Richards.
If you want to make sure you’re hearing the killer new tracks on the GTA 6 soundtrack like the artist intended, you’re going to need a gaming headset that cares about audio quality, like the Stealth™ Pro II Wireless Gaming Headset from Turtle Beach. The Stealth™ Pro II is certified for high-resolution wireless and wired audio, features 60mm Eclipse™ dual drivers that deliver powerful bass and stunning audio detail, and fully immerses you in the game with 3D audio. With the Stealth™ Pro II, you’ll be so lost in the world of Leonida that you’ll forget it’s not even a real place. Which is probably a good thing, since it looks like a lot of things tend to explode there.

articles.chapeau: There are two key reasons gamers are buying "Grand Theft Auto 6" en masse before they
articles.txt:
Rockstar Games Add SVG on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover One of the biggest pop culture events of the new millennium is nearly upon us. The release of "Grand Theft Auto VI" is expected to be an absolute juggernaut. Gamers have been waiting 13 years for the follow-up to "GTA 5," and after many delays, Rockstar is delivering the game mere weeks from now. Pre-orders are through the roof even if the "GTA 6" physical edition doesn't include a disk . But one can't help but wonder: Why are people pre-ordering a game en masse when it hasn't properly been revealed?
Rockstar confirmed a lot about gameplay during the "GTA 6" extended look on Netflix. Up to that point, it had just been a few trailers and a whole bunch of rumors to go off of. But here we are, less than a month away from launch, and we haven't really seen the game properly played. There's so much that has yet to be revealed, especially for a piece of media this high-profile.
The "GTA 6" launch trailer also included some new reveals , but nothing groundbreaking. So, that brings us back to the question: Why are people still preordering a game they haven't fully seen in action, and seemingly doing so happily? There are multiple reasons, but it boils down to two things: FOMO, and Rockstar's history as a gaming studio. Those alone are enough to get a great many people to pull the trigger.
Rockstar Games Undoubtedly the biggest factor is fear of missing out on what is expected to be a global cultural event. It's going to make the release of movies like "Avengers: Endgame" or "Star Wars: The Force Awakens" look like child's play. That may sound dramatic, but it absolutely isn't an overestimation of what's about to go down.
Some reports have claimed that the release of "GTA 6" could cost the U.S. economy $1 billion in just one day , but regardless of the dollar amount, you can bet that many people will be taking the day off to play the game as soon as it launches. If a movie makes $1 billion during its entire run at the box office, that's a huge deal. This game is going to have a multi-billion-dollar global footprint within days — not weeks.
In addition to the FOMO, on a more practical level, there are also some pre-order bonuses for "GTA 6" which sweeten the pot for players. For those who pre-order the Ultimate Edition, there is a "Vintage Vice City Pack" and a free month of GTA+ on offer. All of the pre-orders come with special revolvers, personalized weapon variants, exclusive Vice City outfits, special Safe House vehicles, and more. That's a lot to miss out on for consumers who are fairly certain they're going to buy the game anyway. So why not get the most out of it with a pre-order?
Rockstar Games The other major factor beyond the video game itself is the company behind it. Rockstar Games has a truly ridiculously great track record of pleasing their fans. Yes, that absolutely includes the "Grand Theft Auto" franchise, dating back to its inception. "Grand Theft Auto III" was one of the games from 2001 that changed gaming forever , shifting from a top down approach to an open world format and helping to make the franchise what it is today.
But there are plenty of great Rockstar games that aren't "GTA," and that's the bigger point. "Red Dead Redemption" and "Red Dead Redemption 2," in particular, are amongst some of the most beloved games of the 2010s. Rockstar has a track record of taking what worked before and building on top of it to produce something even more impressive, more immersive, and more satisfying. That's why buying a copy of "GTA 6" not quite sight unseen, but certainly not fully revealed, isn't terribly concerning for a lot of folks.
In the digital era, scarcity isn't really a thing, but anyone who wants a physical edition (even without a disk) might perceive a level of scarcity. That too may be motivating some of the pre-orders. But ultimately, it comes down to Rockstar's legacy of delivering generational games and wanting to be in on the shared cultural event of the year, if not the decade. Those are great reasons to throw down some hard-earned money on a game prior to release.
"Grand Theft Auto VI" releases for PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series X|S on November 19, 2026. The PC release is coming at a later date.

articles.t: Ahead of GTA 6, PlayStation 5 Sales Were Up 22%, Likely Due To Wolverine
articles.chapeau: The latter part of 2026 has been packed with excellent games, all leading up to GTA 6 on November 19, so it's not surprising that PS5 sales have jumped over last month.
articles.txt:
The latter part of 2026 has been packed with excellent games, all leading up to GTA 6 on November 19, so it's not surprising that PS5 sales have jumped over last month.
PlayStation 5 sales have jumped by 22%, according to a report from Bloomberg, with data from Circana. And, while it's likely that the buildup to GTA 6 has contributed to those sales, it looks like it was September's all-star lineup of games, and particularly Marvel's Wolverine, that were primarily behind the PS5's recent success.
We reached out to Circana Senior Director and Video Game Industry Advisor Mat Piscatella for comment on these recent sales increases, and he told us that despite its middling reception, Wolverine drove quite a bit of hardware sales. "PS5's hardware boost was primarily driven by Marvel's Wolverine. NBA 2K27 and Grand Theft Auto VI also likely helped," he said. However, he added that "Xbox Series did not get a similar sales boost during the month."
When IGN reviewed Wolverine, we gave it a middling 6 out of 10, with reviewer Simon Cardy saying, "Marvel's Wolverine's slick and satisfying combat wears thin well before its conclusion, so much so that even its strong character work can't quite save it from being anything more than okay."
In the weeks that have followed the game's release, the community has also been mixed on the game, and Insomniac has had to respond by fixing some of the more hand-holdy mechanics, like adding a toggle for the ever-present scent trail that guides you to objectives . But, even early on, there were signs that Wolverine was selling .
Now, more than a month after release, Wolverine seems like it was absolutely a success, with Piscatella saying, "For Marvel's Wolverine, [it's] tough to give things a vibe check without understanding folks' frame of reference, but it was the month's best-seller, ranks 11th year-to-date, with a hardware bundle that seems to have sold out and the market's best-selling accessory during the month with the limited edition Marvel's Wolverine DualSense. Seems pretty good to me. But, we'll have to see how the legs are over time. It wasn't as big as say Marvel's Spider-Man 2, but I don't think that would have ever been a reasonable assumption."
That hardware bundle was likely a big reason why PlayStation's sales were so rosy over the last month. The controller looked amazing, and started selling out before the game even launched.
Looking ahead to GTA 6, though, if a game like Wolverine was able to drive hardware like this, I can only imagine that GTA is going to make an even bigger impact. We've already started to see signs of that happening, too. Just a couple of weeks ago, the PS5 Pro started selling out enough that used models started going for as much as $1,400, $500 more than their shelf price. And, to this day, that price still holds, with the PS5 Pro available on both Amazon and Gamestop for $1,399.
At that price, it's going to be interesting to see sales data for this coming month, and how many people are willing to fork over that kind of cash for a new console. After all, there have been rumors this week that the next-generation Xbox Project Helix may cost up to $1,800 . There were also leaks that suggest that for the PS6, just the RAM and SSD alone will cost around $680 , which could see Sony's next-gen console commanding a similar price.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.t: "For most of development, GTA 3 was in a sorry state": Rockstar veteran reflects on 25 years of Grand Theft Auto ahead of GTA 6, says "I don
articles.chapeau: If they were fun, they were in. The story was secondary.
articles.txt:
(Image credit: Rockstar Games) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Ahead of GTA 6 , Rockstar veteran Obbe Vermeij marked the 25-year anniversary of Grand Theft Auto 3 with a lengthy retrospective examining its difficult development.
GTA 3 was a pioneering open-world game and a landmark release for Rockstar, but in a recent Twitter post, Vermeij says, "For most of development, GTA 3 was in a sorry state."
Vermeij says "it crashed frequently, the frame rate was terrible and the map was full of holes. Only in the last six months did everything come together. For the longest time, it looked like the frame rate was going to be 20 fps. Only in the final months did we manage to hit 30."
This sort of late assembly is pretty common in game development, particularly among large teams who may have siloed disciplines handling projects of larger scope. In the messy intersection of art and technology, the heart of a game may be hard to see until it's relatively close to release. For example, Bethesda boss Todd Howard said in 2023 that it took seven years for Starfield to become something that's actually fun to play.
Vermeij notes that the beginning of GTA 3 was messy, too. Rockstar North, then operating as DMA Design, had just been snapped up by Take-Two Interactive, "and a satellite office had opened in Edinburgh. Space Station Silicon Valley for the N64 had been finished in 1998, but there was no new project lined up. Leslie Benzies and Aaron Garbut started working on GTA 3. Unprompted. Meanwhile, the original GTA 1 and GTA 2 team had started work on GTA 2.5, set in Miami. It was called 2.5 because it used the 2.5D (isometric) perspective."
What would have been GTA 2.5 was canned in 2000, that Dundee office closed, and GTA 3 was finally officially greenlit by Take-Two and Rockstar, Vermeij adds. "Everything was written from scratch," he explains. "Only two people worked on both GTA 2 and GTA 3, and no code or art from GTA 2 was reused."
"The way we worked was organic. People would come up with ideas for missions and we'd just try them. If they were fun, they were in. The story was secondary. In fact, the opening plot involving Catalina trying to kill Claude was added well into development."
Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more
Back when GTA teams were still pretty small (and downright tiny by today's standards), Vermeij says, "Working on GTA 3 was a lot of fun. Every day there was something new going in. A new mission, radio station, car, pedestrian, building or whatever. The game was growing at an incredible rate. Other than the multiplayer mode we did some work on, I can’t remember a lot of wastage."
Contrast this with GTA 6, which Rockstar admits stalled during development due to conflicting, evolving, or unclear creative visions. GTA 6 hasn't actually been in full production for all of the 13 years since GTA 5, but it did eat up incomparably more labor hours than Rockstar's original breakout hits. With its new development pipeline now stress-tested, studio leadership says future games won't be as difficult or time-consuming to make as GTA 6.
Vermeij also touches on the studio's reputation for crunch – something Rockstar leadership and staff have worked to tackle out in the open in recent years . At least on GTA 3, Vermeij says, "Although everybody worked hard, I don't remember many people doing crazy hours. On the rare occasions I was in over the weekend, there were usually only one or two others. Even during crunch time, most people left the office around 9 or 10 in the evening. I always thought it was better to work eight focused hours than spend your life in the office."
What did all that work get them? Pre-release anxiety. GTA wasn't always the unstoppable hit-maker it is today, and GTA 3 presented a major and risky shift in gameplay. "Although we liked the game," Vermeij says, "it wasn't at all clear that it would be a hit. GTA 3 had a disappointing showing at E3 in May 2001. Most people weren't interested, and those who were thought it was too violent. It had an OK launch, but sales never tapered off."

articles.txt: Grand Theft Auto 6 devs Rockstar had a "dark" period of time during the game's development during 2019-2022, not only because of COVID-19, but also just balancing the realism and the fun, absurd aspects of the game. GTA 6 takes a lot of systems from Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar's last big title. These systems also focused a lot on the realism aspects that the game is now known for. But GTA takes it a step further with very photorealistic graphics, advanced wanted-level systems that include investigations, and a whole relationship simulator where you can take your partner on dates, hold their hand, and more.

articles.t: IGN Is Partnering with Best Buy for 3 Weeks of Giveaways Leading Up to GTA VI’s Release - IGN

We should all be well aware by now that Grand Theft Auto VI is going to take the world by storm when it releases on November 19. It’s widely expected to be the biggest launch in gaming history and one of the biggest launches of any piece of entertainment. Countless people will be taking the day off (or will coincidentally be feeling very sick), leading to that day being the world’s biggest out of office.
Well, IGN is teaming up with Best Buy to celebrate the big day with three weeks of giveaways that can upgrade your setup and get you prepared to play GTA VI in style. That includes TVs, headsets, controllers, soundbars, monitors, and more. It’s thousands of dollars worth of prizes, and you’ll have a chance to win them.
The way it works is simple. Every weekday from October 26 to November 13, we’ll add a new giveaway to the IGN Rewards page, starting with a brand-new PlayStation Portal. Monday–Thursday will feature one new item every day, and all you have to do is log in, click on the sweepstakes, review the Terms & Conditions*, and click “Enter.” That’s it.
Each week will then build up to Friday, when we’ll have a grand prize that’s a themed bundle of multiple awesome things. Like the Do Not Disturb bundle, which includes an LG 65-inch Class C6 OLED TV, an LG S60TR Soundbar and Subwoofer set, Govee Dreamview TV Light Strips, and a copy of GTA VI’s soundtrack on vinyl. Entering the single item giveaways will automatically enter you into that week’s big grand prize drawing.
This all leads up to an event at Best Buy’s store in Torrance, California on November 14, where it’s unveiling a new gaming experience that lets you play the latest releases. IGN will be on hand and filming some content for our social media channels, so drop by and say hi. We’ll also be having an in-person giveaway at the event, so there’s even more incentive.
For the California natives, we hope to see you there. For everyone, best of luck winning the awesome prizes we’ll be giving away. Don’t miss out!

articles.t: Poll: Are You Taking Time Off for GTA 6?
articles.chapeau: USA set for a massive financial hit on 19th November
articles.txt:
We're now less than a month away from the arrival of GTA 6 , and according to recent reporting , its launch day alone may cost America $1 billion.
That's because an estimated 1.5 million workers are planning to take 19th November 2026 as a day off, allowing them to fully immerse themselves in Jason and Lucia's adventure throughout the day.
Assuming the number is accurate, the US economy stands to lose a considerable amount of money in the span of 24 hours.
Interestingly, though, that $1 billion loss in output might balance out, because Rockstar Games' parent company, Take-Two Interactive, expects its current fiscal year to pull in over that amount in operating cash flow. GTA 6 is the main driver behind that.
So, while employers around the country lose a day of labour from a portion of their staff, it seems Take-Two will be banking a similar amount of money anyway.
However you slice these estimates, I think it's quite clear that a lot of people are planning to take at least one day off work (or call in sick) for GTA 6. The amount of hype surrounding Rockstar's latest game is unparalleled.
I saw someone on X (sorry for the lack of credit, whoever you are) compare GTA 6's release to what happens in Japan whenever a new Dragon Quest game comes out — the country basically shuts down so everyone can get the chance to play it on launch day.
Anyway, GTA 6 is fast on the approach now, and I'm curious: are you planning on taking some time off work to dive head first into the open world title?

articles.t: Morning Business Report: Treasury targets home investors as GTA 6 launch could cost $1 billion
articles.chapeau: New restrictions on large home investors are set for January, while GTA 6 could trigger $1 billion in lost productivity and fraud losses among older Americans continue rising.
articles.txt:
(LILAMAX)- The U.S. Treasury Department is moving to restrict large private investors from purchasing additional single-family homes in an effort to improve housing affordability.
Under the announced restrictions, investors who own more than 350 houses would be prohibited from purchasing additional single-family properties beginning January 7. The measure is intended to increase housing availability for individual buyers and help address affordability concerns.
Meanwhile, the upcoming release of Grand Theft Auto 6 could have a significant impact on workplace productivity. The highly anticipated video game is scheduled for release November 19, with some economic estimates suggesting its launch could cost the U.S. economy as much as $1 billion in lost productivity. According to the International Business Times, as many as 1.5 million workers could call out sick or take time off on release day.
On Wall Street, technology stocks declined amid renewed concerns about the sustainability of investments in artificial intelligence. Investors shifted money into consumer products companies, helping Procter & Gamble record its strongest trading day in six and a half years.
In consumer protection news, financial losses reported by Americans ages 60 and older increased 25% in 2025 compared with the previous year. According to the Federal Trade Commission, only 6% of older fraud victims reported losing $100,000 or more, but those cases accounted for 70% of the age group’s total reported losses. Officials say scammers are increasingly targeting older Americans’ savings by impersonating banks, businesses and government agencies.
A new survey also highlights growing feelings of loneliness among Generation Z. Research conducted by Talker Research for Life Time found that seven in 10 Gen Z respondents feel more lonely and isolated than they expected to experience as adults. The survey of 1,000 respondents examined how young adults maintain social connections while navigating adulthood.
On average, participants reported feeling lonely four days a week, even when spending time around other people.
The findings suggest that while social connections remain important to Gen Z, many young adults are finding it more difficult than expected to build and maintain relationships.

articles.t: Activision prépare un monde ouvert XXL pour concurrencer GTA 6 et Cyberpunk 2077
articles.chapeau: Activision prépare un retour en force dans le domaine des mondes ouverts. Le nouveau studio Elsewhere recrute actuellement pour un projet ambitieux axé sur un gameplay émergent ...
articles.txt:
Ajouter aux sources préférées L'éditeur américain Activision, principalement connu ces dernières années pour ses expériences linéaires à grand spectacle comme la franchise Call of Duty, semble prêt à changer son fusil d'épaule. Loin des couloirs scriptés, l'entreprise planche sur un projet de monde ouvert particulièrement ambitieux . Pour mener à bien cette mission, Activision s'appuie sur Elsewhere, un tout nouveau studio composé de vétérans de l'industrie ayant fait leurs armes chez des géants comme CD Projekt Red et Naughty Dog. L'objectif est de proposer une expérience capable de rivaliser avec les mastodontes du genre, que ce soit Grand Theft Auto VI ou Cyberpunk 2077 .
Le cœur de ce nouveau projet repose sur ce que l'on appelle le gameplay émergent. Une récente offre d'emploi publiée par le studio Elsewhere vient confirmer cette orientation. L'équipe est à la recherche d'un directeur adjoint de l'animation dont le rôle sera déterminant pour donner vie à cet univers.
Dans sa description de poste, le studio précise ses attentes :
Le gameplay émergent désigne une conception où les différents systèmes du jeu, qu'il s'agisse de l'intelligence artificielle, de la physique ou des règles de l'univers, interagissent de manière organique et non scriptée . Contrairement à une scène cinématique prévue à l'avance, les événements se produisent naturellement lorsque ces systèmes se rencontrent. Chaque joueur vit ainsi une aventure unique, générée par ses propres actions et les réactions imprévisibles de l'environnement.
Grand Theft Auto est souvent cité comme le meilleur exemple de ce type d'interactions. Une simple bousculade avec un passant peut dégénérer en une fusillade sans qu'aucune ligne de code n'ait spécifiquement écrit ce scénario.
Le titre d'Elsewhere semble également s'inspirer de la réactivité d'un Red Dead Redemption 2 ou d'un Cyberpunk 2077 . Les PNJ pourraient se souvenir de vos actions passées, l'environnement pourrait conserver les stigmates de votre passage, et certains ennemis pourraient même chercher à se venger, à l'image du célèbre système Nemesis de La Terre du Milieu : L'Ombre de la Guerre.
Si le studio Elsewhere ne cherche pas nécessairement à copier ou à terrasser Rockstar Games, il affiche l'ambition de se faire une place de choix dans ce secteur ultra-concurrentiel . Il s'agit d'un véritable changement de cap pour Activision. Pour retrouver la trace d'un véritable jeu en monde ouvert édité par la firme, il faut remonter à l'année de sortie de Prototype, il y a une quinzaine d'année.
Ce projet s'inscrit dans une restructuration plus large des ambitions de l'éditeur. En parallèle de ce monde ouvert inédit, Activision a récemment pris les rênes du développement du prochain opus de la saga Halo , avec la promesse de bâtir l'épisode le plus abouti de la franchise. Le paysage vidéoludique des prochaines années s'annonce particulièrement riche pour la filiale de Microsoft, à condition qu'elle ne soit pas trop touchée par les licenciements.
Ajouter aux sources préférées Corentin Rimbert (Corentin) Les jeux vidéo m'ont toujours accompagné, depuis mon enfance. D'abord avec les consoles portables, telles que la GameBoy Advance et la Nintendo DS, qui m'ont suivi durant une partie de ma jeunesse,...

articles.t: La pub télé de GTA 6 garde les armes mais coupe le baiser et oublie la Xbox
articles.chapeau: La première publicité télévisée de GTA 6 aux États-Unis reprend la bande-annonce de lancement, remontée pour le salon. Ce qu'elle retire, du bracelet électroniq
articles.txt:
Ajoutez-nous sur Google La première publicité de GTA 6 diffusée à la télévision américaine ne contient aucune nouvelle image. Il s’agit de la bande-annonce de lancement de Rockstar, raccourcie pour le petit écran, et c’est justement ce montage qui retient l’attention. Ce qu’un studio choisit de retirer pour s’inviter dans les salons en dit long sur la façon dont il veut présenter son œuvre au public.
Les coupes vont toutes dans le même sens. Le baiser sous la douche entre Jason et Lucia a disparu, tout comme le bref plan sur l’écran du bracelet à la cheville de Lucia. Les armes, les braquages et les courses-poursuites en voiture, eux, sont toujours là. Le carton final affiche une seule marque de console, alors que GTA 6 n’est pas une exclusivité.
Ci-dessus, la bande-annonce de lancement mise en ligne par Rockstar le 15 octobre, dont la publicité télévisée reprend une version raccourcie. Le public a découvert ce montage le 20 octobre, pendant la retransmission par NBC du match entre les Philadelphia 76ers et les New York Knicks, lors de la soirée d’ouverture de la saison NBA. Des enregistrements ont été publiés quelques minutes plus tard. Un fan a indiqué que la publicité était passée au moins deux fois pendant le même match, rapporte The GTA 6 News, et Kotaku précise que d’autres l’ont vue, ou en ont vu une version très proche, lors des rencontres Pistons–Celtics et Thunder–Spurs ce soir-là. Rockstar n’a annoncé aucune campagne télévisée et n’a pas commenté cet achat d’espace publicitaire.
Après comparaison de l’enregistrement télévisé avec la bande-annonce en ligne, RockstarINTEL énumère les différences. Le premier plan sous la douche est conservé, mais pas le baiser qui suit. Pour combler les coupes, certaines séquences existantes durent légèrement plus longtemps : Raul Bautista qui danse, Lucia qui saute sur le train d’atterrissage d’un avion, Jason qui pousse Lucia vers le sol, ou encore Jason qui attrape un couteau alors qu’il la tient dans une prise d’étranglement. Une version plus courte, de 60 secondes, circule également. Rockstar Report résume la situation sans détour : il s’agit d’un montage alternatif, pas d’une nouvelle bande-annonce, et la page des bandes-annonces de Rockstar propose toujours la version en ligne.
La plupart des médias ont rangé cette modification au rayon de la pudibonderie. Le résumé de Kotaku était lapidaire : les armes, les explosions et les braquages passent à la télévision, mais pas les jambes nues sous la douche. Cette lecture vaut pour le baiser. Elle ne tient pas pour la seconde coupe. Le bracelet électronique n’a rien d’intime : c’est une information, un détail que TalkEsport interprète comme le signe que Lucia est en liberté conditionnelle.
Une fois ce détail supprimé, le spectateur installé dans son canapé découvre une héroïne dont le passé judiciaire lui échappe. L’image est plus lisse, mais aussi moins riche. Rockstar n’a expliqué aucune de ces deux coupes. Quelle qu’en soit la raison, leur effet sur l’image est le même.
La publicité se termine uniquement sur le logo PlayStation , sans même mentionner Xbox dans les mentions légales, selon TalkEsport, qui cite TheGamer et le compte de fans videotech. Ce choix s’inscrit dans l’opération de co-promotion autour du slogan « plays best on PS5 » de Sony. La bande-annonce de lancement en ligne ne mentionnait pas non plus Xbox sur son carton final, tandis que Trailer 2, en mai 2025, affichait les deux logos.
Pour les joueurs, rien n’a changé concernant les plateformes. GTA 6 sortira simultanément sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. TalkEsport souligne toutefois le risque que le spectateur occasionnel, voyant un seul logo pendant un match de basket, en conclue que le jeu est une exclusivité PlayStation.
Le montage destiné à la télévision n’est pas la seule version locale. À Paris, l’immense bâche reproduisant la jaquette sur l’une des tours des Mercuriales a été débarrassée de deux armes : le pistolet de Lucia, ainsi que la main qui le tient, et un fusil d’assaut. Les fresques murales aux États-Unis, elles, ont conservé leurs armes, rapporte Kotaku. On ignore qui a décidé de cette modification et pour quelle raison. Mises côte à côte, les deux versions se répondent : la publicité américaine garde les armes et supprime l’intimité, tandis que la façade française retire les armes.
La publicité ne change rien à la date de sortie. GTA 6 arrivera le 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar a fixé le prix de l’édition Standard à 80 dollars e

articles.t: GTA 6 pourrait rompre la tendance en remportant les TGA 2026 — cela est lié aux ventes des jeux gagnants des années précédentes
« GTA, le jeu no limit » : un documentaire à voir avant la sortie de GTA VI
articles.chapeau: Pour la sortie de GTA VI, France.tv diffuse un documentaire inédit sur la franchise, raconté par Fadily Camara, « GTA, le jeu no limit ».
articles.txt:
Après plus d’une décennie d’attente, GTA VI sort très bientôt . Pour cette occasion, France.tv et France 4 diffusent un documentaire inédit sur la franchise de jeux vidéo Grand Theft Auto , raconté par Fadily Camara, GTA, le jeu no limit .
« Alors que GTA 6, le jeu vidéo le plus attendu de l’histoire déferlera sur la planète en ce mois de novembre 2026, plongez au cœur de l’histoire d’un titan de la pop culture ! En trente ans, Grand Theft Auto, désormais connu sous l’acronyme GTA, est passé du statut de paria rejeté par la classe politique et les médias à celui d’œuvre iconique incontournable.
Ce documentaire événement décrypte les rouages d’un succès sans équivalent. Plus qu’un divertissement, GTA s’affirme comme une parodie de l’Amérique consumériste , un miroir de nos tabous et le marqueur d’un nouveau langage artistique . Au-delà de la fresque historique, le film décrypte une fascinante boucle culturelle : en trente ans, GTA a pioché dans le cinéma, le rap et les séries pour finir par devenir lui-même l’un des plus grands piliers de la pop culture mondiale. Le documentaire met en lumière toute l’ ambivalence de ce phénomène, capable de critiquer férocement le modèle américain tout en s’en nourrissant . »
La principale richesse du documentaire est l’ensemble des témoignages de certains qui ont permis à la licence la plus populaire du monde de naître. On a notamment droit aux interviews de Keith Hamilton, Paul Farley ou encore Gary Penn, trois pionniers du studio écosssais DMA Design, qui a créé le premier opus . Vient ensuite Jamie King, qui n’est rien de moins qu’un des cofondateurs de Rockstar Games, aux côtés des frères Dan et Sam Houser.
De quoi revenir sur les prémisses de Grand Theft Auto , du premier concept à la création du nom en passant par l’accueil des premiers épisodes. Puisque oui, on parle évidemment des polémiques dans GTA, le jeu no limit : celle du hot coffee, de la propagande anti-police, etc. On en profite aussi pour revenir sur les influences cinématographiques et musicales de la licence (la filmographie de Martin Scorsese, la funk, le rap américain, etc.). Entre ça et les témoignages des créateurs, c’est ça la vraie force de ce documentaire.
Le documentaire parle aussi de nous, la société, extérieure au jeu, accro parfois. Que ce soient les trends TikTok, le sexisme du jeu (et de son reflet de la société), son rapport aux États-Unis, etc. Tout est bon pour raccrocher le jeu à ce qui se passe dans le monde réel, et vice-versa. Un mélange qui fonctionne assez bien ici, quoique souvent traité en superficie (et en même temps, 52 minutes c’est assez court pour raconter des décennies).
À lire également : Voici les radios qu’on pourra écouter dans GTA VI
Si on sent que les monteurs du documentaires ont adoré travailler sur cette petite histoire d’une grande licence, il y a des choses regrettables. Notamment l’utilisation d’outils d’intelligence artificielle générative pour certains visuels : portraits façon GTA ou pochettes d’albums pour illustrer les musiques du jeu. Au-delà de l’aspect éthique, c’est surtout assez laid parfois.
En bref, rappelons qu’il s’agit d’un documentaire destiné au grand public : si vous connaissez déjà bien l’histoire de GTA, de Rockstar Games et les jeux de la licence, vous n’apprendrez pas grand-chose. Et c’est tout à fait normal ; mais certains détails pourraient vous faire rester dessus.
GTA, le jeu no limit est d’ores et déjà disponible gratuitement sur la plateforme France.tv jusqu’au 9 avril 2029 et sera diffusé le jeudi 12 novembre à 22h40 sur France 4 à l’occasion de la sortie de GTA VI . Et surprise : il est même en ligne sur YouTube :

articles.t: FIFA, GTA VI et "kidultes" : Daniel Riolo dézingue les gamers de plus de 30 ans sur RMC
articles.chapeau: Le 22 octobre 2026, dans Estelle Midi, Daniel Riolo vise les « kidultes » qui jouent encore aux jeux vidéo à 35 ans. Alors que 40 millions de Français manette en main, où commence réellement le problème pour ces adultes gamers ?
articles.txt:
Le 22 octobre 2026, dans Estelle Midi, Daniel Riolo vise les « kidultes » qui jouent encore aux jeux vidéo à 35 ans. Alors que 40 millions de Français manette en main, où commence réellement le problème pour ces adultes gamers ?
Dans Estelle Midi sur RMC et RMC Story , le 22 octobre 2026, Daniel Riolo a relancé un vieux débat : a‑t‑on le droit de rester gamer passé 30 ans. « J’étais à fond sur FIFA , mais je ne pouvais pas m’empêcher de me dire que c’était une perte de temps », lâche le chroniqueur. Avant de viser ceux qu’il appelle les « kidultes » : « Ce qui m’angoisse, ce sont les kidultes ! ‘J’ai 35 ans et je continue à m’abrutir là‑dessus' ».
Autour de la table, l’émission discute d’un chiffre choc : 40 millions de Français jouent aux jeux vidéo . Riolo, ancien ambassadeur de FIFA 13 , assume avoir été accro, mais estime qu’ »il faut passer à autre chose » quand on devient adulte. Alors, jouer à 35 ans, est‑ce vraiment refuser de grandir ou juste un loisir comme un autre.
Dans la séquence « La peur du jour » d’ Estelle Midi , Daniel Riolo raconte ses débuts sur Super Mario et Donkey Kong , puis sa plongée dans FIFA au milieu des années 2000, quand il sert d’ambassadeur au jeu. « Je m’y suis mis et j’étais à fond », reconnaît‑il, tout en affirmant qu’il « perdait du temps sur [sa] vie ». Le chroniqueur dit être surtout « angoissé » par ces adultes qui, selon lui, restent des enfants, jouent « du matin au soir » et remplissent des stades lors de compétitions d’e‑sport. Face à lui, on lui rappelle que c’est « une activité » qui n’est « pas plus condamnable que de faire de la pêche, de la chasse ».
Dans les études marketing citées par l’ ESSCA , un kidulte , contraction de « kid » et « adult », désigne un adulte de 20 à 55 ans qui consomme jeux, jouets, figurines et culture geek, souvent avec un bon pouvoir d’achat. En France, ce public pèse déjà 29 à 33 % du chiffre d’affaires des jeux et jouets, soit environ 1,3 à 1,4 milliard d’euros, avec une part attendue autour de 40 % d’ici 2034.
Côté jeu vidéo, les chiffres du SELL et du Sénat sont clairs : 40,2 millions de Français jouent au moins une fois par an, près de 30 millions chaque semaine, 88 % sont majeurs et l’âge moyen tourne autour de 39 à 40 ans. Statistiquement, le joueur « type » est donc déjà un adulte, pas un ado attardé.
Pour l’ Organisation mondiale de la santé , le « trouble du jeu vidéo » est réel, mais il touche une minorité de joueurs, autour de 3 à 5 % d’usages problématiques selon les autorités françaises. Le critère n’est pas l’âge, mais l’excès : perte de contrôle, priorité donnée au jeu sur le travail, la famille ou la santé pendant des mois. Poser un jour de congé pour lancer GTA VI n’a rien à voir avec un isolement massif où tout le reste passe après la manette. Comme le cinéma ou les séries, le jeu vidéo est un loisir culturel, parfois artistique, qui sert à se détendre, à sociabiliser, à se défouler après le boulot. La vraie question pour les gamers de 30 ou 40 ans n’est pas « suis‑je un kidulte », mais « est‑ce que mon temps de jeu reste compatible avec ma vie d’adulte ».

articles.t: Même GTA 6 n'aurait pas réussi à les avoir ! Un nouveau set LEGO annoncé
articles.chapeau: LEGO a dévoilé une nouvelle collaboration originale, qui marquera une grande première pour un set basé sur un artiste. Et visiblement, même GTA 6 n’a pas réussi à obtenir un partenariat avec eux.
articles.txt:
LEGO a dévoilé une nouvelle collaboration originale, qui marquera une grande première pour un set basé sur un artiste. Et visiblement, même GTA 6 n’a pas réussi à obtenir un partenariat avec eux.
Cette année encore, LEGO a enchaîné les collaborations venues de tous horizons. Du jeu vidéo, des films, de la pop culture, mais également des sportifs et des artistes. Le fabricant de danois s’attaque désormais à un monument de la musique électronique et de la scène musicale française : Daft Punk. Une annonce qui prête forcément à sourire alors que Rockstar aurait envisagé un retour du duo pour la bande originale de GTA 6 et aurait essuyé un refus.
Une fois n’est pas coutume, le nouveau set est devenu possible grâce à l’imagination débordante d’un fan sur LEGO Ideas en 2024. Il est désormais officiel. Le constructeur a en effet révélé sa première collaboration avec Daft Punk qui prendra la forme d’un set inspiré de leur tournée emblématique Alive 2007 et de ses sons emblématiques comme Human After All. LEGO ne compte manifestement pas s’arrêter là et annonce également un partenariat plus large, qui doit s’accompagner d’événements musicaux et créatifs. Si ce n’est pas la première fois que la marque collabore avec des artistes, des sets LEGO ayant déjà été créés pour les Beatles, les Rolling Stones ou encore BTS, c’est bien la première fois que le groupe danois recrée une scène entière d’un artiste. Aucune date de sortie ou prix n'ont été communiqués pour l'heure.
Aperçu de set LEGO Daft Punk Quand le groupe aurait refusé de collaborer avec GTA 6 Pour les joueurs, cette annonce prend une autre dimension au regard des rumeurs entourant GTA 6 . Il se murmure en effet que Rockstar aurait approché Daft Punk afin de proposer au duo de se reformer pour composer la bande originale du jeu, avec un budget qui aurait été présenté comme quasiment illimité. Justice aurait ensuite été le second choix du studio, après avoir essuyé un refus. L’information n’a, évidemment, pas été confirmée par Rockstar et relève toujours de la rumeur. Mais si le duo, séparé en 2021, ne semble pas prêt à reprendre du service, il sera au moins réuni dans ce set LEGO. Le groupe danois promet de communiquer davantage d’informations à son sujet dans les semaines à venir.

articles.t: Avant GTA 6, la PS5 Pro est introuvable partout mais elle est enfin de retour en stock ! Où acheter la meilleure console pour y jouer ?
articles.chapeau: Après plusieurs semaines de pénurie, la PS5 Pro est officiellement de retour en stock. Voici où l’acheter si vous souhaitez profiter de la meilleure version possible de GTA 6.
articles.txt:
Après plusieurs semaines de pénurie, la PS5 Pro est officiellement de retour en stock. Voici où l’acheter si vous souhaitez profiter de la meilleure version possible de GTA 6.
« L’expérience ultime se vit sur PS5 » . Voilà les mots que l’on pouvait lire dès les premiers secondes du dernier trailer de GTA 6 . Car oui, le titre de Rockstar Games n’est peut-être pas une exclusivité PlayStation, mais il bénéficie tout de même d’un partenariat avec la firme, qui entend bien profiter au maximum du séisme que provoquera le jeu dès sa sortie. En sachant que l’une des grandes gagnantes de cette histoire pourrait alors être la PS5 Pro qui, après plusieurs semaines de pénurie, est officiellement de retour en stock.
En effet, courant septembre, PlayStation tirait la sonnette d’alarme en confirmant ce que beaucoup redoutaient : à l’aube de la sortie de GTA 6, il n’y aura visiblement pas de PS5 Pro pour tout le monde. Les deux sont-ils réellement liés ? Pas forcément. Mais cela reste tout de même une fâcheuse situation qui pourrait en frustrer plus d’un. C’est pourquoi il ne vaut sans doute mieux pas tarder à passer à l’action si vous désirez jouer à la meilleure version possible du jeu de Rockstar, car ça y est : la console est enfin de retour en stock chez Micromania.
Notez toutefois que contrairement à la PS5 standard, le socle permettant de placer la console debout est vendu séparément, au même titre que le lecteur de disques blu-ray pour ceux qui souhaiteraient soutenir les jeux physiques jusqu’au bout. Et si vous en faites partie, voici deux boutiques où vous pourrez notamment vous en procurer un :
Avec cela, vous serez alors prêts à jouer dans les meilleures conditions possibles au prochain hit de Rockstar Games, dont la sortie est officiellement attendue pour le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series. Et au vu de tout ce que nous avons pu en voir jusqu’à présent, mais aussi de toutes les déclarations faites par ses créateurs ces dernières semaines, on peut probablement d’ores et déjà s’attendre à l’un des jeux en monde ouvert les plus impressionnants de sa génération. Un monde ouvert dont, on l’imagine, il sera possible de tirer tout le meilleur sur PS5 Pro.

articles.t: Grand Theft Auto 6 : la bande-annonce de sortie que vous attendiez
articles.chapeau: L’attente est terminée, et le résultat s’annonce prometteur.
articles.txt:
Rockstar Games franchit l’une des toutes dernières étapes d’un très long parcours : la bande-annonce de lancement de Grand Theft Auto 6 est arrivée jeudi. Dans une saga aussi populaire que chaotique, cette nouvelle vidéo se distingue des précédentes, notamment grâce à un nouveau morceau envoûtant de Justice, avec Tame Impala, SZA et King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard. On adore absolument tout.
À en juger par la bande-annonce, l’attente semble en avoir valu la peine. Cette vidéo de lancement adopte un ton que les autres jeux de la série n’avaient jamais vraiment atteint. Cela fait presque un an que Rockstar Games a annoncé la sortie de GTA 6, et nous nous rapprochons désormais de sa date de lancement fixée au 19 novembre sur Xbox Series X, Series S et PlayStation 5.
L’histoire se concentre sur un personnage nommé Jason, un ancien militaire qui reconnaît s’être « attiré quelques ennuis » et explique que « les gens comme moi n’obtiennent pas de prêt ». Lorsqu’il reçoit un appel de Lucia, l’autre personnage central, l’histoire démarre et nous plonge dans l’aventure et le chaos que le jeu cherche à proposer.
GTA a toujours été une sorte de jeu où chacun peut choisir sa propre aventure. Personnellement, je n’ai jamais suivi les scénarios jusqu’au bout, préférant profiter de la liberté offerte par le monde ouvert pour faire ce que je voulais dans un environnement très vaste. Mais cette bande-annonce a éveillé ma curiosité et me donne envie de savoir ce qui va arriver à nos personnages principaux.
Le nouveau morceau en fond sonore est à la fois dynamique et mélancolique, ce qui laisse penser que l’histoire à venir ne se résumera pas à un simple jeu de destruction et de chaos.
GTA 6 est en développement depuis extrêmement longtemps — GTA 5 est sorti en 2013 — et nous allons enfin pouvoir découvrir le résultat de toutes ces années de travail chez Rockstar Games. Préparez-vous à une nouvelle aventure qui devrait séduire aussi bien les fans de longue date de GTA que les nouveaux venus.

articles.t: Cyberleek Threatens GTA 6 Build Leak Over Discs And An Apology
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek says a GTA 6 build leak will happen at a 30M market cap unless Take-Two ships physical discs and apologises. We look at what’s actually known.
articles.txt:
GTA 6 has spent years being picked apart by leakers, and now one of them is threatening to go much further than just sharing footage. Cyberleek has said on his website that he’ll release a playable build of the game to the public once he hits 30 million in market cap, as spotted in a post on r/GamingLeaksAndRumours . This GTA 6 build leak threat comes with conditions attached, and TakeTwo is the one being asked to meet them.
It is worth noting that none of this has been verified and there’s no confirmation that Cyberleek actually has a build, and neither Rockstar nor TakeTwo has responded publicly.
Cyberleek also acknowledged that the publisher probably assumes he’s bluffing and that’s a fair assumption on TakeTwo’s part, given that he hasn’t shown anything publicly that proves he has a build to release.
The market cap part is the strangest element. Market capitalisation usually refers to the total value of a company’s shares or a cryptocurrency token, but the post doesn’t say what asset this figure applies to, what currency it’s measured in or who controls it. Without that, it’s impossible to tell how close he is to the target, or whether the whole thing’s tied to some kind of token promotion.
The physical disc condition suggests Cyberleek is positioning himself as speaking for players rather than simply holding a game to ransom. The post doesn’t explain the reasoning, though, or what TakeTwo has done that he thinks warrants an apology.
Disc ownership has been a sore point across the industry for a while. More big releases are shipping as download codes or with only part of the game on the disc, and plenty of players see a physical copy as the only version they truly own. Whether that’s what’s driving this demand isn’t clear from what’s been shared.
If Cyberleek is bluffing, he’s picked a target where leaks are easy to believe. Rockstar’s history includes the 2022 breach that put early GTA 6 development footage online, and the hacker behind that is set to go back to court just days before the game launches . Older material keeps surfacing too, with stolen GTA 5 files revealing cancelled single-player expansions .
There’s a big difference between leaking video and leaking a working build, though. Footage spoils surprises. A build in the wild could be datamined for every mission, map area and system Rockstar’s spent years developing, and it’d give cheat makers a head start before the game even goes on sale.
For anyone on PC hoping a leak means getting hands on GTA 6 early, it’s worth being sceptical. Supposed leaked builds of huge games are a common lure for malware, because people are willing to download large archives from unknown sources and run whatever’s inside.
Even if a genuine build did appear, there’s no indication of what platform it’d be for or how complete it’d be. Development builds are often unstable, unoptimised and tied to specific hardware or tools, so it’s far from guaranteed anyone could run one on a normal gaming PC.
If something does surface claiming to be GTA 6, the safest move is to leave it alone. A compromised system isn’t a fair trade for an early look at a game that’s coming anyway. For now, this looks more like an attention grab than a credible threat, especially with that unexplained market cap target attached.
Do you think Cyberleek actually has a build, or is this a bluff aimed at hype? Let’s know your thoughts in the comments.

articles.txt:
Lire sur mobile Avant même sa sortie fixée au 19 novembre, Grand Theft Auto VI cumule déjà 6,45 millions d'achats anticipés en version dématérialisée, générant environ 630 millions de dollars de revenus nets. Sans surprise, la console de Sony écrase la concurrence en captant 74 % des volumes globaux face à une machine Microsoft en retrait. Les chiffres compilés par le cabinet d'analyse Sensor Tower jusqu'au 20 octobre donnent le ton à tout un secteur. À un mois de son arrivée dans l'État fictif de Leonida, le mastodonte de Rockstar Games et Take-Two Interactive affole tous les compteurs mondiaux. En une seule semaine, 370 000 joueurs supplémentaires ont sécurisé leur copie numérique, faisant bondir la cagnotte de 594 à 630 millions de dollars . Cette ruée massive s'explique par une attente de plus d'une décennie depuis le précédent volet et un engouement démesuré pour les éditions premium du jeu .
En s'accaparant très exactement 74 % des parts du gâteau sur le marché dématérialisé, la playstation laisse sa rivale directe ramasser les miettes d'un festin pourtant historique. Concrètement, cela représente 4,80 millions de copies sécurisées sur l'écosystème nippon, soit une manne financière de 468 millions de dollars .
En face, la xbox doit se contenter de 26 % des volumes, totalisant tout de même 1,66 million d'exemplaires pour 162 millions de dollars générés. Ce déséquilibre reflète fidèlement la dynamique matérielle actuelle, les machines de Sony se vendant dans une proportion de trois contre un face aux consoles Series X|S, dont les ventes américaines touchent le fond cette année. Le ratio de 2,8 copies réservées chez Sony pour une seule chez Microsoft apparaît dès lors presque logique.
Le volume actuel des précommandes numériques sur le sol américain surpasse de 148 % le précédent détenteur du record sur les six dernières années, un certain Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II en 2022, observé exactement au même stade avant sa commercialisation. Des poids lourds du calibre de Cyberpunk 2077 , Elden Ring, Spider-Man 2 ou Hogwarts Legacy sont relégués au rang d'amateurs sur les graphiques de suivi. Cette domination insolente ne tient même pas compte des ventes physiques en magasin .
Plus fascinant encore, les joueurs refusent de compter leurs sous. La courbe isolant uniquement le SKU (Stock Keeping Unit, soit une référence d'article précise dans un catalogue commercial) affiché à 99,99 dollars dépasse seule les ventes totales de n'importe quel autre blockbuster suivi depuis six ans. Si le PDG Strauss Zelnick se frottait déjà les mains en août devant l'attrait pour cette Ultimate Edition, l'absurdité culmine avec le coffret collector à 399,99 dollars vendu sans le jeu , preuve ultime que Rockstar peut absolument tout se permettre face à un public hypnotisé. Le titre standard, lui, réclame déjà 79,99 dollars au passage en caisse.
Le raz-de-marée ne fait que commencer. L'impact culturel et financier de grand theft auto 6 dépasse largement le cadre du divertissement habituel, poussant les studios concurrents à déserter le mois de novembre et incitant même certaines bases militaires à offrir des permissions de sortie comme prime de réengagement. Un pic d'achats massif est d'ailleurs attendu dès le 12 novembre prochain , date d'ouverture du préchargement des fichiers sur les consoles.
Les projections financières donnent le tournis aux analystes de Wall Street. Tandis que le cabinet Piper Sandler table sur un écoulement compris entre 45 et 48 millions d'unités dès la semaine de lancement, les experts de Newzoo estiment que le titre pourrait engloutir jusqu'à 5,2 milliards de dollars sur cette même période initiale. De quoi rembourser instantanément une décennie de développement extrêmement coûteux.
Le téléchargement anticipé des données du jeu sera accessible dès le 12 novembre prochain sur PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series X|S, soit exactement une semaine avant la sortie officielle fixée au 19 novembre .
La version standard est commercialisée à 79,99 dollars , tandis que l'édition Ultimate s'affiche à 99,99 dollars . Un coffret collector rempli d'objets dérivés est également proposé à 399,99 dollars , mais il n'inclut aucune copie du jeu.
Non, les 6,45 millions d'unités et les 630 millions de dollars générés sont des estimations tierces fournies par le cabinet d'analyse Sensor Tower. Elles ne couvrent que les achats numériques mondiaux , excluant totalement les réservations de disques physiques.

A claim traced to the social-media account Has It Leaked says Rockstar Games asked Daft Punk to score Grand Theft Auto VI and got a no. Dexerto relayed the story under a headline saying the duo reportedly turned down the Daft Punk GTA 6 soundtrack deal despite an “unlimited” budget. The original post is dated October 19, 2026. Nothing in it has been confirmed by anyone who would actually know.
Rockstar has made no official comment on the alleged negotiations. No statement confirming the offer or the rejection has come from Daft Punk or its representatives. What is confirmed sits right next to the rumor, and that is why the story travels so well: Justice created the original score for the game, and a Daft Punk member is credited on a track tied to the game’s album.
This analysis sorts the claim into what is verified, what is rumor, and what it could mean for a release already carrying heavy expectations. The timing matters because spending pressure on blockbuster games is a live debate, as our recent look at GTA VI budget fears and the cost of AAA scale showed. A music story built around the phrase “unlimited budget” lands squarely in that conversation, whether or not it holds up.

The rumor has five moving parts. First, that Rockstar Games approached Daft Punk about the Grand Theft Auto VI soundtrack. Second, that the pitch was framed as a “final comeback” for the duo. Third, that the proposed budget was essentially unlimited. Fourth, that Daft Punk said no. Fifth, that Justice became Rockstar’s second choice.
Every one of those five points is unconfirmed. They arrive as a bundle, which gives the story a satisfying shape: a legendary act refuses a blank check, and a French house peer steps in. Neat narratives deserve extra suspicion. A rumor with a clean beginning, middle and end is easier to share than a messy one, and it is also easier to invent.
Daft Punk split in 2021, so any reunion pitch would have asked the pair to undo a decision they made publicly. That context makes the “final comeback” wording feel plausible to fans, but plausible is not evidence. The duo has no obligation to answer rumors, and silence here tells readers nothing in either direction.
Outlets covering the story have mostly used careful verbs. “Reportedly” appears in the Dexerto headline, and the NME headline uses the same hedge. That framing is the right one, and it is the one this article follows throughout.

Notice how the confirmed rows and the rumor rows interlock. Justice really did the score, so “second choice” sounds natural. A Daft Punk member really is credited on a related track, so “they were in the building” sounds natural too. Rumors that borrow real furniture feel stronger than they are.
The reporting chain begins with a post from the account Has It Leaked on October 19, 2026. Even that origin is listed as unconfirmed in our verification notes, which means readers should treat the attribution itself with care. Several outlets have pointed to the same account, but pointing to the same account is not the same as independent confirmation.
This is a classic loop. One post makes a claim, a gaming outlet writes it up with a “reportedly,” other outlets write up the first outlet, and the volume of coverage starts to feel like corroboration. By the time the story reaches a search results page, a dozen headlines carry the same unverified core. MusicRadar’s headline handles this well by posing the whole thing as a question rather than a statement.

(Image credit: Rockstar/Tripping Animals Brewing) Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Now this is a marketing campaign I can get behind: It looks very much like Rockstar is teaming up with Florida-based brewery Tripping Animals Brewing to bring a trio of Grand Theft Auto 6 -themed beers into the real world. That's right— Pißwasser is finally real.
The discovery was made by Grand Theft Auto site GTAVice.net , which found labels for Pißwasser, Patriot, and No Mames Vice City—a re-branding of Tripping Animals' No Mames Lager—in the US Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau database .
Sure enough, they're in there, although I had to use Hopgrail to dig up the labels: The No Mames Vice City label was approved on October 9, while the Pißwasser and Patriot labels followed on October 15.
This looks to be a re-brand of Tripping Animals' No Mames beer, so here's what the brewery's website has to say about it: "Bright gold and effortlessly crisp, No Mames blends flaked corn and traditional malts for a smooth, dry lager with subtle floral hops and a hint of sweetness. Clean, crushable, and brewed for easy drinking, anytime."
Patriot and Pißwasser are not yet on the Tripping Animals site, so for those we will go with what we can pull from the TTB database, which frankly isn't much:
A very American lager, the GTA Fandom Wiki says Patriot Beer is possibly inspired by Sam Adams, although it notes that the color scheme of the label is more akin to PBR. Personally I think it's more likely a prescient take on Real American Beer , which is basically a GTA-style parody beer, except it's real. Real American .
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
The king of GTA beers, Pißwasser is of course a pilsner, it says so right on the label. Now, your local beer nerd is probably leaning forward in his chair to tell you that pilsner is a type of lager, but my local beer nerd, who is me, says that yes, that is technically correct, but it's important to be specific about these things. Otherwise you get people telling you that Rolling Rock and Warsteiner are basically the same, and next thing you know you're in a fistfight with Bill from your grade 10 geography class and then somebody calls the cops and you end up running through people's back yards and tripping over shit and ripping your pants, and nobody gets any beer. Who needs that kind of chaos?
Anyway, none of these brews are confirmed as actually happening at this point, although given their appearances in the TTB database, not to mention Rockstar's largesse with its rental of basically the entire state of Florida to promote GTA 6 , it's all but certainly real. It's also an obvious fit, particularly given the meta-popularity of GTA's in-game beer brands.
The bigger question for me is, how do I get some? Promo beers tend not to be great, but No Mames holds a very respectable 85 rating on Beeradvocate , and Tripping Animals seems quite well regarded overall. And let's not forget the all-important bottom line here: it's beer .
Sadly for me (and anyone else not living in Florida who'd like to score a few cans) Tripping Animals distribution appears quite limited: The brewery's website indicates its beers are only available in and around—you guessed it—Miami. Ah well.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is set to launch on consoles on November 19. I would expect the GTA beers to show up by then too.

articles.chapeau: Cyberleek posted a three-part End of the road message on Oct 14, 2026, ending its GTA 6 leak campaign without a PC build or spoilers.
articles.txt:
Cyberleek, the anonymous account behind months of Grand Theft Auto VI leaks, says it is done. On October 14, 2026, the leaker posted a three-part message titled “End of the road,” announcing it will not release a full game build, will not post the game’s ending, and does not plan further early gameplay leaks. The post marks the clearest signal yet that the long-running GTA 6 leak saga, which has rattled Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two Interactive for the better part of a year, may finally be winding down.
Whether that holds is a separate question. Cyberleek has reversed course before, and nothing in the latest message can be independently verified beyond the post itself. Still, the announcement reframes a leak campaign that previously threatened to dump an entire playable build onto torrent sites. Instead, the leaker is walking away, at least for now, while keeping a handful of final-mission clips online as what it calls proof of access.
Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
According to the October 14 post, Cyberleek broke its farewell statement into three distinct parts. The first addressed the fate of the alleged full game build, the second covered the ending and story content, and the third offered a handful of final clips described as proof rather than spoilers. Kotaku reported on the message under the headline “GTA 6 Leaker Announces They Won’t Release The Full Game” , framing it as the leaker calling a stop to the campaign, at least for the time being.
Cyberleek had previously floated a conditional threat: if a crypto token tied to the account hit a $30 million market cap, the full build would go out, story mode included, all the way to the credits. In its own words from that earlier post, “Here’s the deal, nice and clean. CYBERLEEK hits 30 million marketcap, the build goes out, full story mode, played to the end, credits and all,” as Gadgets360 reported at the time. That target was never reached, and the October 14 message closes the loop on it.
Cyberleek’s stated reasoning centers on risk versus reward. Uploading hundreds of gigabytes of a stolen build anonymously carries real exposure, and the leaker framed the payoff as only worth it if the crypto milestone had funded whatever project sat behind the threat. With the target missed, the math apparently stopped working. The account has made no claim about a PC build timeline, pricing, or file size beyond what it has already posted, and none of those specifics are confirmed by any outlet covering the story.
This is a notable shift from the tone Cyberleek struck in earlier posts, which read more like negotiation tactics aimed at Take-Two than a farewell. Eurogamer covered the escalation at the time the full-build threat first surfaced, and the contrast between that posture and the October 14 retreat is stark. Readers can track the earlier claim in shattered.io’s own coverage of Cyberleek’s 200GB “playable” build claim , which laid out the scope of what the leaker said it was holding.
The second part of the message dealt specifically with the game’s ending, and it’s arguably the most consequential piece of the whole statement. Cyberleek claims to have access to the conclusion of GTA 6’s story but says it will not publish it. In its own words, reported by Kotaku, “CL has the ending. It was considered. It would punish Take-Two greatly, but ruin the experience for the gamers, who did nothing wrong. Take-Two would show CL no mercy, why should CL show any to them? Still: Take-Two was punished enough. The ending stays unpublished.”
That framing matters because it draws a line between punishing a publisher and punishing the people who bought the game. Cyberleek positions itself as drawing that line deliberately, rather than being forced into it. No outlet has confirmed whether the claimed ending footage actually exists, and Take-Two has not addressed the claim directly.
The third part of the message included clips Cyberleek describes as coming from the game’s final missions. The leaker characterized them in its own words as “the latest leek, clips from the final missions, out of context, revealing nothing,” according to Kotaku’s report. The framing suggests the footage is meant to demonstrate continued access rather than deliver new story information, a distinction Cyberleek has drawn consistently across its various posts this year.

articles.txt:
GTA 6 Trailer Features 'Dacity' Meme Coin—Here's What Traders Think It'll Do Ryan Gladwin Wed, October 21, 2026 at 8:16 AM CDT 3 min read SOL-USD -1.49% The recent Grand Theft Auto 6 launch trailer briefly mentioned a "Dacity Coin," and crypto traders are speculating on how involved the apparent meme coin will be in-game. Some believe it'll feature in a few side missions, while others believe it'll be a fully tradeable in-game asset.
In response, crypto degens have created an unofficial Solana meme coin of the same name and pumped it to a peak market capitalization of $15 million. Traders say they are essentially gambling on the prominence of Dacity Coin in GTA 6, believing that if it is deeply integrated, it'll lead to bigger gains—despite the Solana token having no official ties to the game.
"I think there will be some missions related to Dacity Coin where [GTA 6 protagonist] Lucia will need to promote it to earn money," pseudonymous meme coin trader Nicstho told Decrypt . "This is the classic thesis."
This theory is corroborated by leaked gameplay of an apparent mission, released more than a week ago by notorious Rockstar hacker "Cyberleek." According to the GTA wiki, Lucia is asked to parachute as a stunt to attract investment to the Dacity Coin.
"Give them a show. They'll buy Dacity Coin before they even know what it is," someone tells Lucia on the phone during the mission, according to a leaked screenshot.
In the official launch trailer, a wing walker sets off a smoke bomb atop a plane plastered in Dacity Coin branding. This has led some traders to believe that the Dacity Coin could be featured in multiple missions, with the player tasked with performing crazy stunts to pump the token—just like real-world meme coin traders have done in the past.
Dacity Coin also appears to be connected to an in-game brand called AudaCity, with AudaCity featuring in both the leak and trailer alongside the coin. It appears that AudaCity is the company behind the Dacity Coin, per the GTA wiki.
Some traders believe that the meme coin will feature more heavily than just a couple of side missions. Nicstho said that the bull thesis is that Dacity Coin is an in-game currency that can be spent both in single-player and multiplayer, adding that would be "huge" for the real-world Solana token—despite there being no official link between the two.
"I guess you'll be able to trade it like you trade stocks on GTA V," pseudonymous meme coin trader Corey Ape told Decrypt . "Just think the last GTA you could buy any of the stocks from the mission on the game, you can probably do the same here."
Corey Ape said that this is purely gut instinct, but it makes sense. In GTA V's single-player story mode, gamers could invest in stocks in an attempt to get rich quick—entire investment guides were created around this feature. Corey Ape believes it is only natural for an in-game meme coin to be tradable by gamers, after Rockstar set this precedent in the last game.
"Obviously the [real-world] coin hasn't been launched by Rockstar," Nicstho said. "They just want to mog memecoin traders."
As rumours and speculation continue to swirl, the real-world Solana token has soared. One trader has unrealized profits of $285,000 from just a $20,000 investment, according to trading platform Pump.fun. Though it's important to stress none of this is realized and it could sharply fall at any moment, as is the nature of meme coins .
A section of crypto traders are now eagerly awaiting GTA 6's November release, hoping it'll pump their bags.
